item.title: Frasers increases Burberry stake again as it expands luxury interests
item.description: British retailer Frasers has further increased its stake in luxury brand Burberry to 7.42%, having already raised its holding at the end of September, as the Mike Ashley-controlled company broadens its interests in the luxury sector.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: British retailer Frasers has further increased its stake in luxury brand Burberry to 7.42%, having already raised its holding at the end of September, as the Mike Ashley-controlled company broadens its interests in the luxury sector. The owner of Sports Direct is known for aggressively buying up retailers, and in August [USN:L6N44A0S4 TEXT:"bought"] luxury department store Harvey Nichols out of administration, as well as pursuing a [USN:FWN4530VJ TEXT:"takeover"] of Hugo Boss. Frasers had on September 30 disclosed a stake of 6.32% in Burberry, up from 4.16% previously. Its stake is held entirely via sold put options with expiries of October 2026, March 2027, and September 2027. Burberry declined to comment, and Frasers did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the increased stake. Frasers last week set out a luxury strategy, saying it sees opportunities to expand its department store chain Flannels in Europe and Harvey Nichols globally.

item.title: Starbucks says not buying Chipotle, ends takeover speculation
item.description: Starbucks is not buying Chipotle Mexican Grill , the coffee chain said on Monday, quashing talk of a deal that could have been the largest-ever involving restaurants but was doubted by both investors and analysts.
item.dc:creator: Anuja Mistry, Neil Kanatt
item.content:encoded: Starbucks (SBUX.O) is not buying Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG.N) , the coffee chain said on Monday, quashing talk of a deal that could have been the largest-ever involving restaurants but was doubted by both investors and analysts. "As a matter of policy, we don't comment on rumors and speculation, but we want to be clear we are not buying Chipotle," a Starbucks spokesperson said. Chipotle declined to comment. The statement follows [USN:L6N45U0YK TEXT:"a report by the Financial Times on October 8"] that Starbucks had worked with advisers in recent months on a potential proposal to acquire Chipotle, citing people familiar with the matter. Starbucks did not respond to a request for comment on whether they approached advisers for a deal. Shares of the coffee chain were up 1% in early trading, while Chipotle, whose shares surged on the prospect of a takeover which would have reunited Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol with the burrito chain he led for six years, fell about 4%. Starbucks also reiterated that its management was "laser focused" on "Back to Starbucks" strategy and had "strong momentum and confidence" in its long-term growth prospects. The company aims to share its fourth-quarter results and fiscal 2027 outlook later this month. Starbucks shares have gained 7.8% this year, roughly half the gain in the S&P 500 over the period. The chain has been closing [USN:L4N45G0UG TEXT:"dozens"] of underperforming stores as part of a turnaround led by Niccol, who has tried to draw back customers with shorter wait times and simpler menus. TAKEOVER SPECULATION The report of a potential deal last week prompted the investor community to speculate about a tie-up that would have brought together two of the largest US restaurant brands. Chances of a deal sent Chipotle shares up more than 7% and Starbucks down about 3%, even as several analysts questioned the strategic rationale as Starbucks was in revival mode under Niccol. "Rumors like these can prime investment bankers to start fantasizing about all sorts of tie-ups, but they're a tough sell. The tide has been shifting more toward divestitures than acquisitions," From Brian Jacobsen, chief economic strategist at Annex Wealth Management said. A potential deal would have created a restaurant giant with about $50 billion in annual sales, positioning it to better navigate uncertain demand from inflation-hit consumers, rising operating costs and the squeeze on profits. The burrito chain has a market capitalization is around $40 billion. NICCOL'S CHALLENGE "Funding a premium takeover price would likely require a mix of debt and equity, which would test leverage and could dilute existing shareholders while Starbucks is still executing its turnaround," Paren Knadjian, Partner at Transaction Advisory Services, EisnerAmper said last week. Niccol joined Starbucks in 2024 after leading Chipotle through a period of rapid growth and digital expansion. He was credited with reviving the burrito chain after its food-safety crises and expanding its digital business, helping accelerate sales growth. Chipotle, meanwhile, has grappled with softer traffic as consumers cut back spending, while higher food and labor costs hurt margins across the restaurant industry. Their shares have nearly halved in value since Niccol's departure.

item.title: イラン、米回答なお精査中 イエメン危機解決に協力の用意
item.description: [ドバイ １２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ドバイ １２日 ロイター] - イラン外務省のバガイ報道官は１２日、ホルムズ海峡の再開に関するイランの提案に対する米国の回答は依然精査中だと述べた。精査が終わり次第、仲介者を通じて米政府に返答するとしている。

バガイ氏は、イランは仲介者を通じてメッセージのやり取りを続けているとも述べたが、詳細には触れなかった。

イラン最高安全保障委員会のレザイ事務局長は、米国の回答は「不十分」だったと述べた。国営メディアが１１日報じた。

サウジアラビアとイエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派の衝突が激しくなっていることについて、バガイ氏は、対話による危機の解決に協力する用意があるというイラン政府の立場を改めて示した。

「イエメン問題は（国連の）ロードマップ（行程表）によってずっと前に解決しているべきだった。われわれは、イエメンとサウジの間で成立するいかなる合意も支持すると表明していた」とし、対話を通じた解決を望むと述べた。

Oct 12 : Global smartphone shipments fell 20 per cent on-year to their lowest third-quarter level since 2012, as soaring memory chip costs and supply shortages pressured manufacturers and pushed up prices, preliminary estimates from Counterpoint Research showed on Monday. Rising prices for memory components as AI infrastructure projects corner supplies have driven up production costs and prompted manufacturers to raise retail prices, cut shipments and prioritize profitability over volumes. "Consumers are holding on to their devices longer than estimated, increasingly considering refurbished devices and prioritizing higher-value devices," said Counterpoint senior analyst Shilpi Jain. Samsung retained its top position with a 23 per cent market share, helped by demand for its Galaxy Z Fold8 series and stable component supplies for its mid-range devices. Shipments fell 3 per cent from a year earlier during the quarter.

Apple's market share reached 22 per cent, crossing 20 per cent for the first time in a third quarter, despite a year-on-year decline in shipments. The absence of a base iPhone 18 model resulted in a smaller launch-month channel fill than the full iPhone 17 lineup a year earlier, Counterpoint said. OPPO and vivo recorded shipment declines of more than 20 per cent. Xiaomi saw a more than 30 per cent fall, reducing its market share to 10 per cent as the company cut exposure to lower-priced devices and some overseas markets to protect margins. "The outlook for the remainder of 2026 remains challenging," Counterpoint said. "Production cuts, tighter portfolios, and greater focus on premium devices are likely to continue, while price-sensitive segments face further pressure from higher device prices and limited availability of components."

item.title: サウジ首都の空港が閉鎖延長、フーシ派攻撃で被害 経済への影響懸念
item.description:
Gianluca Lo Nostro Menna AlaaElDin
［１２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Gianluca Lo Nostro　Menna AlaaElDin

［１２日　ロイター］ - サウジアラビア当局は１２日、週末にイエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派の攻撃を受けた首都リヤドのキング・ハリド国際空港の運用停止措置を延長した。

サウジ民間航空当局は、空港閉鎖について、「空港施設の安全と運用準備態勢を確保するための手続きを完了させる」ためだと説明した。

同空港の利用者数は、ジッダに次いで国内２番目に多い。一連の攻撃は、サウジ航空業界に混乱をもたらすとともに、航空燃料の高騰に直面している航空会社にさらなる打撃となっている。

航空データ分析会社シリウムによると、同空港では１２００ＧＭＴ（日本時間午後９時）時点で予定されていた全便の８２％が欠航となっている。最終的な数字はさらに高くなる可能性があるという。サウジ国内の全空港での欠航率は４６．４％に達した。

航空機追跡サイト「フライトレーダー２４」のデータによると、航空機は１２日、リヤドを避けて飛行している。ただ、サウジ領空を通過し、西海岸の主要拠点であるジッダに着陸する便は見られた。

混乱を受けて欧州やアジアの航空各社は運航停止を余儀なくされている。欧州航空安全庁（ＥＡＳＡ）は９日。ミサイルや無人機（ドローン）による攻撃を理由に、サウジ領空に関する警告の対象範囲を拡大した。米連邦航空局（ＦＡＡ）は１１日、米国の航空会社に対し、サウジへの飛行や領空通過の際に警戒するよう勧告した。

ルフトハンザ・グループはリヤド便を１０月１６日まで全便欠航とし、エールフランスＫＬＭはリヤド発着便の運航停止措置を今月末まで延長した。

アブダビのエティハド航空もサウジ便の欠航延長を決め、１２日と１３日にリヤド、ジッダ、ダンマンを結ぶ約２０便に影響が出た。

今回の攻撃は、今月リヤドで開催予定の大規模会合にも影を落とす。世界石油会議（ＷＰＣ）の会合は、複数の石油大手トップが参加を取りやめた。

フーシ派との衝突激化により、より広範な経済的影響への懸念が強まっている。サウジの実質国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）は、石油活動の低迷など複数の要因を反映し、２０２６年に３．６％縮小すると予測されている。

item.title: Bergs stuns Alcaraz in Shanghai as Zverev claims year-end top ranking
item.description: Seven-times Grand Slam champion Carlos Alcaraz suffered a shock 7-5 7-6(4) defeat by unseeded Belgian Zizou Bergs in the Shanghai Masters round of 32 on Monday, a result that also confirmed Alexander Zverev as the ATP's year-end world number one.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Seven-times Grand Slam champion Carlos Alcaraz suffered a shock 7-5 7-6(4) defeat by unseeded Belgian Zizou Bergs in the Shanghai Masters round of 32 on Monday, a result that also confirmed Alexander Zverev as the ATP's year-end world number one. Fresh from defending his [USN:L1N45S0G0 TEXT:"Japan Open"] title and building momentum after a wrist injury that sidelined him for nearly five months, Alcaraz never found his rhythm in a scrappy two-hour, two-minute contest. The second-seeded Spaniard joined 24-times Grand Slam champion [USN:L1N45V0DT TEXT:"Novak Djokovic"] and US Open runner-up [USN:L4N45X01T TEXT:"Ben Shelton"] among the high-profile casualties at the ATP Masters 1000 event. Bergs produced a composed all-court performance, thriving in the quick conditions as the 27-year-old broke Alcaraz's serve three times to clinch the biggest victory of his career. Bergs had lost their only previous meeting, falling to Alcaraz in the last 16 of last year's Japan Open, but showed no signs of intimidation as he outplayed the 23-year-old in key moments. "I often have too much respect for these guys, which is part of my culture and I'm proud of that. But it gets a little bit in the way when you have to play them...," Bergs said. "The more experience you have practising against them and playing matches, the more it becomes the new standard a little bit. To have this moment, for me it is a little bit of a relief. I feel like now I really can win against these guys..." Alcaraz conceded he was below his best. "I didn't play the way that I wanted to play. A lot of mistakes. I didn't find a good position on the return," Alcaraz said. "Obviously, credit to him. I would say he served really well. "But when I got into the rhythm, when I got into the point, I made a lot of mistakes. I wasn't feeling comfortable with my shots. So, I'm really disappointed with today's match because I didn't find the solution. I just made a lot of unforced errors." 'DREAM COME TRUE' The upset also guaranteed French Open and US Open champion Zverev, 29, the ATP's year-end world number one ranking, making him the first German and the oldest first-time player to achieve the feat. Zverev's rise to year-end number one was aided by the absence of five-times Grand Slam champion [USN:L1N45S0CV TEXT:"Jannik Sinner"], who has not played since beating the German in the Wimbledon final in July due to a knee injury and will miss the rest of the season, including the ATP Finals in Turin. "It's been a fantastic season for me winning in Paris and New York and knowing that I will finish the year on top of the rankings is just a dream come true," said Zverev, who will face Kazakhstan's 19th seed Alexander Bublik in the round of 16 in Shanghai. "So much work and effort have been put into achieving this goal, especially after coming back from the ankle injury (at the 2022 French Open semi-finals). "I look forward to finishing the season in style."

item.title: Le pape Léon XIV hospitalisé mardi, ses engagements annulés jusqu'au 20/10
item.description: Le pape Léon XIV sera hospitalisé mardi matin en vue d'une intervention chirurgicale visant à retirer un petit nodule situé dans l'un de ses poumons, a indiqué lundi le service de presse du Vatican.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le pape Léon XIV sera hospitalisé mardi matin en vue d'une intervention chirurgicale visant à retirer un petit nodule situé dans l'un de ses poumons, a indiqué lundi le service de presse du Vatican. Tous les engagements publics du saint-père sont en conséquence annulés jusqu'au 20 octobre. Le souverain pontife, âgé de 71 ans, a annoncé dimanche que cette excroissance à un stade précoce avait été détectée lors d'un récent bilan de santé et qu'elle était "bien circonscrite". Le Vatican n'a pas précisé la date à laquelle l'opération du pape aurait lieu.

item.title: Papa Leone sarà ricoverato domani mattina - Vaticano
item.description: Papa Leone sarà ricoverato in ospedale domani mattina in vista dell'intervento chirurgico per la rimozione di un piccolo nodulo al polmone.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Papa Leone sarà ricoverato in ospedale domani mattina in vista dell'intervento chirurgico per la rimozione di un piccolo nodulo al polmone. Lo ha riferito l'ufficio stampa del Vaticano. Papa Leone, 71 anni, ha detto ieri che un piccolo nodulo è stato individuato durante una recente visita di controllo, che è "ben localizzato" e in fase molto iniziale. A causa del ricovero tutte le udienze fino al 20 ottobre sono state annullate, secondo quanto riferito dal Vaticano in serata.

Oct 12 : Italian Giulio Ciccone has signed a three-year contract with Pinarello Q36.5, the Swiss team said on Monday, after the 31-year-old mutually parted ways with Lidl-Trek after eight seasons. Ciccone's last race in the Lidl-Trek colours ended with a third-placed finish in Saturday's Giro di Lombardia, after the team announced his departure on the eve of the race despite still having three years left on his contract. "After eight years with the same team, this is a big decision, but one I genuinely wanted to make," Ciccone said in a Pinarello Q36.5 statement. "I feel I still have a lot to give, and I needed a new challenge, fresh motivation and an environment where I could feel at home."

item.title: US immigration authorities raid Democratic congresswoman Ilhan Omar's home
item.description: US authorities conducted a predawn raid on Monday on the Washington-area home of Democratic US Representative Ilhan Omar of Minnesota, an outspoken critic of Donald Trump who has been the target of political insults by the Republican president, as part of an ongoing investigation, the Justice Department said.
item.dc:creator: Nolan Mccaskill, Andrew Goudsward, Doina Chiacu
item.content:encoded: US authorities conducted a predawn raid on Monday on the Washington-area home of Democratic US Representative Ilhan Omar of Minnesota, an outspoken critic of Donald Trump who has been the target of political insults by the Republican president, as part of an ongoing investigation, the Justice Department said. A person familiar with the investigation said it is related to alleged immigration fraud, and part of the probe concerns the Somali-born lawmaker's immigration paperwork, which was filled out by her late father when she was a child. Omar wrote in a social media post that the US government is being weaponized to target a political enemy of the president. "For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns," Omar said. "This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced." Other Democrats accused Trump and his administration of abuse of power. Omar, 44, is seeking a fifth two-year term in the US House of Representatives in the midterm elections on November 3. In announcing the raid, a Justice Department spokesperson said: "Today in the Washington, DC area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice. This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal investigation." Homeland Security Investigations is part of US Immigration and Customs Enforcement, or ICE. Tom Homan, the Trump administration's border czar, told Fox Business Network that the Justice Department is leading the investigation with the Department of Homeland Security. Homan declined to get into the specifics of an ongoing criminal investigation. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, a Trump appointee, said last month that "something's gonna happen" in the investigation into Omar's family's entry into the United States. "If we can prove that you shouldn't have been here in the first place, we'll deport you," Mullin told conservative podcaster Benny Johnson at the time. Monday's raid was carried out a little more than three weeks before the midterms, with Trump's party seeking to retain control of Congress. Omar, a prominent progressive, represents a safe Democratic district. She won reelection in 2024 by a margin of 50 percentage points. DEMOCRATS CONDEMN RAID In a joint statement, US House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries and other members of the party's leadership in the chamber said the raid was "deeply disturbing and raises serious questions about the" weaponization of the federal government against Trump's enemies. Republicans have "relentlessly targeted" Omar, said Jeffries, joined by Representatives Katherine Clark and Pete Aguilar. Trump's "mass deportation machine has descended upon the home of a duly elected Member of Congress and her family," they added, and they vowed to "deliver full accountability" for what they called a "rogue abuse of power." Minnesota Democrats also condemned the raid. "Americans see this for what it is," Minnesota Governor Tim Walz, a Democrat, wrote on social media. "President Trump is abusing his power to go after political opponents weeks before an election." Justice Department policy bars federal prosecutors and agents from timing any action to affect the outcome of any election or benefiting a candidate or political party. The department has historically avoided taking investigative steps against political candidates within about 60 days of an election. INVESTIGATIONS OF TRUMP CRITICS The Justice Department during Trump's second term in office has investigated and brought charges against a range of Trump's perceived political enemies. It has charged former FBI Director James Comey, New York state Attorney General Letitia James and Trump's former national security adviser turned critic John Bolton. It also has investigated Democratic lawmakers who urged the US military not to follow illegal orders, Democratic Senator Adam Schiff and Federal Reserve officials Jerome Powell and Lisa Cook. The case against James and one of two brought against Comey were thrown out by a federal judge. Bolton pleaded guilty and is scheduled to be sentenced later this month. Grand juries and federal judges have stymied several other probes. 'CREEPY OBSESSION' Omar has faced political insults from Trump, who has [USN:L1N45U12W TEXT:"cast"] the Somali American community as a threat to Minnesota in a burst of anti-Somali and anti-Muslim rhetoric. Omar has called Trump's focus on her an "unhealthy and creepy obsession." Last week, Trump called Michigan's Democratic nominee for US Senate — Abdul El-Sayed, who is Muslim — a "RADICAL Extremist" and "Terrorist Sympathizer" while offering support for El-Sayed's Republican opponent, Mike Rogers. Civil rights advocates have criticized Trump's rhetoric toward minorities and immigrants, including when he previously called Somalis "garbage." Trump in February said that Omar and Democratic Representative Rashida Tlaib of Michigan, who is also Muslim, should be "institutionalized" and sent back to "where they came from." Both lawmakers had criticized Trump during his State of the Union address as he touted his administration's hard-line immigration crackdown and its immigration enforcement actions. Omar has said she and her family have faced death threats, which she attributes to "hateful political rhetoric," especially from Trump. Last month, a Minnesota man who squirted vinegar on Omar [USN:L6N4591B6 TEXT:"was sentenced"] to one year and two months in prison after pleading guilty to assaulting a federal official. Anthony James Kazmierczak admitted to attacking Omar because he disagreed with her progressive political views.

UN refugee agency's funding shortfall is impacting refugees worldwide, its chief says

GENEVA: Deep funding shortfalls are forcing the UN refugee agency to make painful cuts across its humanitarian operations worldwide, and there are limits to how much restructuring can offset shrinking donor support, its chief said on Monday (Oct 12). UNHCR has secured only US$3 billion, or 35 per cent of the US$8.5 billion in funding it requires for 2026, High Commissioner Barham Salih told the agency's executive committee at a meeting in Geneva. The shortfall follows aid cuts by countries including the United States under President Donald Trump at a time of record global displacement. Funding for next year remains uncertain although the expected figure of around $2.68 billion could improve after a UNHCR donor pledging conference in December, Salih said.

UNHCR has launched one of its largest restructurings in the agency's history because of the budget squeeze, with Salih saying its workforce had been reduced since 2024 from 20,000 employees to just under 12,000. "Protection has a floor. Below it, the system does not simply become smaller. The protection we can provide begins to fail," he said. Salih cautioned that restructuring could not compensate indefinitely for lower funding, and that the funding crisis was already having tangible consequences for refugees and humanitarian partners. "There is a difference between doing more with less and being asked to do the impossible," he said.

Related:

IN FOCUS: 'I cannot go back' - Myanmar refugees fear repatriation as country gets cosier with Malaysia, Thailand

Number of forcibly displaced people dips to 118 million: UN

JOB CUTS UNHCR is seeking to preserve frontline operations by cutting jobs at its Geneva headquarters and worldwide regional offices, with 88 per cent of staff remaining outside headquarters, Salih said. About 95 per cent of the staff doing protection work, such as registering refugees and providing legal assistance, and helping refugees find longer-term solutions, such as returning home safely, have been retained in field locations, he said.  He cited several examples of programmes under threat.  In Chad, he said, insufficient funding risks disrupting specialised medical care and legal assistance for more than 50,000 survivors of conflict-related sexual violence who fled neighbouring Sudan.  In Ethiopia, refugee registration had been suspended for tens of thousands of refugees from South Sudan and Eritrea, he said. Colombia has raised concerns on behalf of Latin American countries that their region is being disproportionately impacted.  The Americas, which include the US, Canada, Latin America and the Caribbean, face a budget reduction of 32 per cent in 2027 compared to this year, or about $485 million — the largest budget reduction of any region — while the number of forcibly displaced and stateless people in the Americas is projected to increase by 4 per cent to about 24.5 million people in 2027, Salih said.

Source: Reuters/ia

item.title: ＥＵのＨＶ輸入上限枠、中国ＥＶ各社に打撃 欧州現地生産加速へ
item.description: ［上海／北京 １２日 ロイター］ - 中国が欧州連合（ＥＵ）向けのハイブリッド車（ＨＶ）輸出を抑えることに同意した。国内...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＥＵのＨＶ輸入上限枠、中国ＥＶ各社に打撃　欧州現地生産加速へ 10/12 20:33 配信

2026年4月15日、南アフリカ・ヨハネスブルグでのイベントで撮影　REUTERS/Nqobile Dludla/File Photo

［上海／北京　１２日　ロイター］ - 中国が欧州連合（ＥＵ）向けのハイブリッド車（ＨＶ）輸出を抑えることに同意した。国内販売の伸びが鈍る中、中国の電気自動車（ＥＶ）メーカーにとって新たな打撃になる。

中国商務省は１２日、この取り決めで輸出は今後も増やせるとし、中国には他のどの輸入元に割り当てられる枠よりも小さくない数量枠が保証されると表明した。

中国自動車各社は、ＥＵの中国製ＥＶに課す関税の対象外であるＨＶの輸出を増やしてきた。中国税関のデータによると、２０２６年上半期のＥＵ向けＨＶ輸出額は７５億ドルと、前年同期（２５億ドル）の３倍だった。

ジェフリーズによると、上海汽車集団（ＳＡＩＣ）、比亜迪（ＢＹＤ）、奇瑞汽車の３社が、ＥＵで販売される中国製ＨＶの９割超（台数ベース）を占める。３社の欧州販売では、半分以上がＨＶとなっている。

シュミット・オートモーティブ・リサーチによると、欧州ＥＶ市場での中国ブランドのシェアは２６年第２・四半期に過去最高の１５％となった。２４年第１・四半期は９．５％だった。ＰＨＥＶ市場でも中国製のシェアは４分の１を超え、２４年初めのわずか１．７％から急拡大した。

＜現地生産加速へ＞

仏ルノーのフランソワ・プロボ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は１２日、中国製ＨＶの輸入急増は欧州にとって持続可能ではないと述べた。一方で、今回の合意は貿易戦争よりは望ましいとし、通商関係を「賢明に」管理する必要があると指摘した。

投資家はおおむね、今回の合意を貿易摩擦の緩和と受け止め、中国製ＨＶへの関税が当面は見送られる兆しとみている。

シティのアナリストは、実施ルール、数量上限、最低価格などは、今後さらなる協議が必要だが、とりあえずリスクが緩和したと指摘した。

中国の自動車業界に詳しいコンサルタントのマイケル・ダン氏は「中国が合意を守るのか、それとも抜け道や一時的な関税免除を見つけるのか、見ていきたい」と述べた。

アナリストらは、数量枠の制度が始まる前に輸出を前倒しする動きが出る可能性があるが、合意は最終的に、中国の自動車メーカーによる欧州での現地生産を加速させる可能性があるとみる。

上海のコンサルティング会社オートモビリティの創業者、ビル・ルッソ氏は「これで、中国の自動車メーカーが欧州で生産する動機は強まるだろう」と述べた。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：ＥＵのＥＶ補助金巡る対中調査、自らに跳ね返るリスクも コラム：短距離フライト削減でＣＯ2対策なるか、的外れの欧州 焦点：トランプ政権の影で歩み寄るカナダとＥＵ、準加盟提示でも見える限界 焦点：コーヒー企業「アフリカ離れ」も、ＥＵが森林破壊防止法 アングル：長時間労働・残業に不満の中国労働者、ＥＵの対中圧力に「共感」 最終更新: 10/12(月) 20:33 ロイター

item.title: Surfing hotspots around the world are more vulnerable to climate change, says new study
item.description: The research analysed 57 surf breaks across eight countries to arrive at its findings. Each of the sites selected is incorporated into a World Surfing Reserve.
item.dc:creator: Purvi Rajpuria
item.content:encoded:

Surfing hotspots around the world are more vulnerable to climate change, says new study

The research analysed 57 surf breaks across eight countries to arrive at its findings. Each of the sites selected is incorporated into a World Surfing Reserve.

Purvi Rajpuria

12 October, 2026 04:43 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Representative image (c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2024

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

New Delhi: Many of the most prominent surf breaks across the world are vulnerable to climate change, even as the degree and type of vulnerability differ widely, a recent study found.

The study, titled ‘ Globally significant surf breaks are vulnerable to climate change ’, was co-authored by Dan R Reineman of California State University Channel Islands, along with researchers from Save The Waves Coalition and World Surfing Reserves .

The research analysed 57 surf breaks across eight countries to arrive at its findings. Each of the sites selected is incorporated into a World Surfing Reserve (WSR)—“a status applied for by local stakeholders and designated by an international non-profit organization based on each site’s cultural, historical, and environmental significance for surfing,” the study explains.

Show Full Article

These surf breaks, the research found, are vulnerable to climate change, due to changing tide levels, hardened shorelines caused by manmade structures, and shifting sands. Surf breaks rated at most risk include Croyde beach in north Devon, UK, and Oriente Salvaje in El Salvador.

What are surf breaks? Dan Reineman, a co-author of the study, pointed to the several factors that come together to form a surf break. “Surf breaks are incredibly unique oceanographic phenomena – a confluence of all these factors that fit together just right to make the wave happen – and so those processes are really sensitive,” he said .

Some of these factors include swell direction, tide, and intricate combinations of sea-floor shape. Climate change, global warming, and changing rainfall patterns can affect any of these factors, hampering the delicate balance of surf breaks and thus destroying the wave.

Significantly, the study found that coastlines that were more natural and less populated by manmade structures could adapt better to the changes caused by climate change. These coastlines were able to adapt by shifting inland and relocating sediments. Construction of features such as sea walls, jetties and groynes made the beaches and waves less resilient, Reineman said .

Also read: Mamdani has a new target. Subscriptions that make cancellations difficult

Affects local economy at large Climate change-related vulnerability matters not only to surfers, but also to the local people who depend on the multi-billion-dollar surf economy that exists in these sites.

Adam Hall, a co-founder of the North Devon WSR, was one of the local surfers who contributed to the study. Explaining the significance of surfing to the local economy, he said , “Surfers will come throughout the year. They fill up the pubs, restaurants and car parks when the swells are good in January, February and March, where if you go to any other tourist destination that doesn’t have surf, they’re dead on their knees.”

Many of these sites often have little else in terms of local economy.

Local surfers also played a key role in guiding the research. Trent Hodges, a co-author of the study and a senior programmes manager at Save the Waves Coalition, said , “We learned directly from the local surfers how they are seeing their waves change. It’s a canary in the coalmine too – when a wave changes, that often means the beach is changing, and everybody enjoys the beach.”

The study also hypothesises that similar risks could affect other surf breaks, not included in the present research, and encourages other local people and organisations to assess their vulnerability.

(Edited by Ratan Priya)

Oct 12 : Norway's data protection authority has fined Microsoft's adtech unit Xandr 92 million crowns ($9.61 million) for unlawfully relaying Grindr users' sensitive data to thousands of advertisers, it said on Monday. Xandr relayed data revealing the sexual orientation of users of Grindr, a dating app for LGBTQIA+ people, to companies in automated ad auctions from July 2018 to April 2020. It is the biggest fine the Norwegian authority has issued, and targets the advertising middlemen rather than the app itself. The regulator said companies that traded in people's data could not pass the blame to others. The data protection authority fined Grindr 65 million crowns over the same breaches in 2021.

The fine was based on Xandr's revenue, not Microsoft's, which did not own the unit at the time. Xandr has three weeks to appeal. Xandr said it assumed Grindr had obtained users' consent and never checked, the data protection authority said. It rejected that argument and ruled Xandr shared legal responsibility with Grindr.  Microsoft said the privacy of users was a top priority. "This investigation and decision focused on conduct that predates Microsoft's acquisition of Xandr, and in that time the interpretation and application of legal standards and practices has continued to evolve. We are reviewing the decision and assessing our options," it said. The case began with a 2020 complaint by the Norwegian Consumer Council, whose research exposed how apps shared user data, and Austrian data privacy organisation noyb, which called the decision "a valuable precedent".   ($1 = 9.5704 Norwegian crowns)

item.title: FTSE 100 ends higher as financial, medical stocks offset crude price hit
item.description: Britain's FTSE 100 edged higher on Monday, buoyed by financials and medical equipment stocks as investors looked ahead to crucial US inflation data and UK GDP readings due this week for fresh insight into the economic outlook.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's FTSE 100 edged higher on Monday, buoyed by financials and medical equipment stocks as investors looked ahead to crucial US inflation data and UK GDP readings due this week for fresh insight into the economic outlook. The blue-chip FTSE 100 index (.FTSE) rose nearly 1% to 10,656.28 points, while the midcap FTSE 250 (.FTMC) climbed 0.47%. Oil prices jumped 2% to $106.76 a barrel, hovering near two-week peaks, as attacks on Saudi Arabia outweighed prospects of higher supplies from Russia and a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire on energy facilities Attention will also be on UK Finance Minister John Healey's meetings with foreign counterparts on his first trip to the International Monetary Fund's annual meetings this week Healey faces pressure ahead of his [USN:L8N45X047 TEXT:"first annual budget on October 28"], with higher borrowing costs and an estimated £36 billion fiscal gap to address "I will work with our international partners  to keep trade moving, support families and businesses, and make Britain's economy stronger and more resilient," Healey said ahead of his address at the IMF meetings later this week Upper Crust chain owner SSP Group (SSPG.L) shares fell 2.2% after brokerage [USN:L6N45Y0LK TEXT:"Berenberg cut target price"] to £225 from £245 Burberry (BRBY.L) shares rose 1.9% after retailer Frasers (FRAS.L) increased its stake in the luxury brand to 7.42% from 6.32% Financial stocks (.FTNMX301010) were among top gainers: HSBC Holdings (HSBA.L) , Standard Life (SDLF.L) , Lloyds Banking Group , Barclays (BARC.L) , NatWest (NWG.L) , Standard Chartered (STAN.L) gain between 1.7% and 2.3% Medical equipment and services (.FTNMX201020) shares rose 2.75% Market participants are awaiting US inflation data due on Wednesday, while UK GDP figures for August are scheduled for release on Thursday

item.dc:creator: Vishak Mathew
item.content:encoded: Los precios del oro cayeron el lunes tras alcanzar un máximo de una semana a primera hora de la sesión, ya que la fortaleza del dólar y el alza del petróleo lastraron al metal precioso. * Los inversionistas, en tanto, esperan los datos de inflación de Estados Unidos, que podrían modificar las expectativas sobre la trayectoria de las tasas de interés. * El oro al contado bajaba un 0,6% a 4.169,10 dólares por onza a las 1745 GMT, tras alcanzar su nivel más alto desde el 2 de octubre a primera hora de la sesión. Los futuros del oro estadounidense con entrega en diciembre caían un 0,6% a 4.190,60 dólares por onza. * "Estamos observando cierta presión vendedora sobre el oro porque el dólar se encuentra cerca de su máximo en un año y medio", afirmó Jim Wyckoff, analista de mercado de American Gold Exchange. * La escalada del conflicto en Oriente Medio mantuvo a los inversores en vilo a la espera de los datos clave sobre la inflación en Estados Unidos de esta semana, que influirán en la política monetaria. * El reporte del Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) de Estados Unidos se publicará el miércoles, seguido del Índice de Precios al Productor (IPP) y de los datos de ventas al por menor el jueves. * Los mercados han reducido sus apuestas por una subida de tasas de interés de la Fed este mes; según la herramienta FedWatch de CME, los operadores descuentan un 18% de probabilidades de que se produzca una subida este mes, aunque siguen viendo un 88% de probabilidades de que se produzca una subida en diciembre. * En un entorno de tasas de interés elevadas, los inversionistas tienden a preferir los activos que generan rendimiento frente al oro. * El petróleo subió a cerca de máximos de dos semanas ya que los ataques contra Arabia Saudita eclipsaron la posibilidad de un aumento de la oferta en el mercado, después de que el presidente Donald Trump, acogiera con satisfacción las nuevas exportaciones rusas de gasóleo y el alto el fuego energético entre Rusia y Ucrania. * Entre otros metales preciosos, la plata al contado caía un 1% a 60,22 dólares por onza; el platino bajaba un 0,2% a 1.684,20 dólares por onza; y el paladio caía un 0,5% a 1.141,90 dólares por onza.

item.title: Jury selected for actor Russell Brand's UK trial over sex crimes allegations
item.description: Jury selection took place on Monday for the trial of British actor and comedian Russell Brand over alleged historical crimes including rape and other sexual offences.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Jury selection took place on Monday for the trial of British actor and comedian Russell Brand over alleged historical crimes including rape and other sexual offences. Brand, 51, once one of Britain's most high-profile broadcasters and former husband of US singer Katy Perry, faces three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of indecent assault relating to six women from 1999 to 2009. Brand has denied all the accusations. He arrived at London's Southwark Crown Court wearing sunglasses and accompanied by his wife. During the hearing he sat in the dock, mostly staring straight ahead or with his eyes closed. "We are about to start the trial of one Mr Russell Brand," the judge Joel Bennathan told potential jurors. "Many of you will have heard of him." The judge excluded those who said they had watched a documentary aired about three years ago or had read a long newspaper article from the same time in which allegations of sexual misconduct were made against Brand. "Those are allegations he firmly denies," the judge said. He later told those who had been initially selected: "The defendant is clearly someone very well known. You absolutely must not carry out any research at all about this defendant Russell Brand." The trial is expected to last about six weeks, Bennathan said, with the jurors formally sworn in on Tuesday while prosecutors will open their case later in the week. The comedian, known for his flamboyant style and appearance, was a regular on British television screens in the 2000s and also worked as a radio presenter for the BBC. He went on to star in a number of films including "Get Him to the Greek" in 2010, the same year he married Perry. They divorced in 2012 after 14 months of marriage. More recently Brand has largely appeared on online programmes, with content often focused on US politics, religion and free speech.

item.title: Aluminio repunta desde mínimo de ocho meses y el cobre toca máximo de dos semanas
item.description: Los precios del aluminio tocaron el lunes un mínimo de ocho meses, ya que la fortaleza del dólar ejerció presión sobre el ánimo de los inversores, mientras que el cobre tocó un pico de más de dos semanas por preocupaciones sobre las interrupciones en el suministro de las minas.
item.dc:creator: Polina Devitt
item.content:encoded: Los precios del aluminio tocaron el lunes un mínimo de ocho meses, ya que la fortaleza del dólar ejerció presión sobre el ánimo de los inversores, mientras que el cobre tocó un pico de más de dos semanas por preocupaciones sobre las interrupciones en el suministro de las minas. * El contrato de referencia del aluminio a tres meses en la Bolsa de Metales de Londres (LME) ganó un 0,2%, a 3.054 dólares por tonelada, a las 1604 GMT, tras hallar soporte en los 3.023 dólares, su nivel más bajo desde el 13 de febrero, más temprano en la sesión. * El dólar alcanzó su nivel más alto desde abril de 2025 a la espera de los datos clave sobre la inflación en Estados Unidos que se publicarán más adelante esta semana y que podrían marcar las perspectivas de las tasas de interés. * El aluminio ha caído un 19% desde que tocó un máximo de cuatro años en junio, según se disipaban las preocupaciones sobre las interrupciones del suministro procedentes de la región del golfo Pérsico y crecían las expectativas de una mayor capacidad de producción en Indonesia. * Aunque los bajos niveles de existencias visibles siguen respaldando los precios, es probable que la aceleración del crecimiento de la oferta fuera de China empuje al mercado mundial a un superávit de 1,8 millones de toneladas en 2027, frente al déficit de 941.000 toneladas de este año, según Citi. * Por su parte, el cobre en la LME subió un 0,5%, a 14.616 dólares por tonelada, tras alcanzar los 14.688 dólares, su cota más elevada desde el 25 de septiembre. * Las preocupaciones sobre el suministro se vieron avivadas por una suspensión parcial en la mina El Teniente de Codelco, en Chile, tras un alud que causó la muerte de dos trabajadores el domingo. La huelga en la mina Centinela de Antofagasta, también en Chile, continúa, y está previsto que las negociaciones se reanuden el martes. * En otros metales básicos, el zinc cayó un 1,2%, a 3.757,5 dólares; el níquel cedió un 0,1%, a 15.595 dólares, tras tocar su mínimo desde fines de diciembre, a 15.500 dólares; el plomo bajó un 0,2%, a 1.883,5 dólares; y el estaño sumó un 0,4%, a 53.155 dólares.

item.title: Australia need six wickets on final day to win first test
item.description: Australia's Matt Renshaw played a leading role to leave his side needing six wickets on the last day of the first test to beat South Africa as the hosts were 102-4 at the close of play at Kingsmead on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gleeson
item.content:encoded: Australia's Matt Renshaw played a leading role to leave his side needing six wickets on the last day of the first test to beat South Africa as the hosts were 102-4 at the close of play at Kingsmead on Monday. Set 421 runs to win after Australia declared their second innings on 314-6, South Africa saw opener Ryan Rickelton, David Bedingham, captain Temba Bavuma and Tristan Stubbs all dismissed before stumps with part time spinner Renshaw weighing in with his first test wicket as his dream performance continued. Aiden Markram (45 not out) and Wiaan Mulder, unbeaten on five, will resume on the final morning, needing to lead a stoic rearguard action if the home side are to avoid defeat. "We gave up a couple of soft wickets again but the application Aiden showed is what we are looking forward tomorrow," said veteran spinner Keshav Maharaj. Rickelton’s place in the test side looks under threat after another early dismissal. He was out for a duck after three balls of the first innings and scored two on Monday before an attempted pull shot saw him edge Josh Hazlewood's rising delivery to wicketkeeper Alex Carey. Bedingham was the second wicket to fall, making 46 before being trapped lbw by Hazlewood and ending a patient 66-run partnership with Markram, while Bavuma scored a single run, prodding at Renshaw's off spin and being caught bat-pad at short leg. Stubbs also made one, getting a thick edge to captain Pat Cummins' delivery with another example of the poor shot selection that has dogged South Africa's batting. "It's been a good last two days for us," said Australia's Beau Webster. "We've still got a job to do tomorrow but given ourselves a great chance." RED-HOT BATTING FORM Earlier, Renshaw continued his red-hot batting form to allow his side to declare at tea, picking up where he left off in the first innings when he scored 190 of Australia's 390 runs. The 30-year-old Queenslander continued to dominate the home bowlers, scoring 82 in the second innings before a controversial caught and bowled from Maharaj ended his contribution. It was the top score for Australia, who accelerated their run accumulation in a bid to give themselves time to put South Africa into bat and chase down the 10 wickets required for victory. They resumed on 33-0 and scored 141 runs in a fast-moving first session for the loss of four wickets and a further 140 in the afternoon. CAPTAIN CUMMINS IN WHIRLWIND BATTING DISPLAY Opener Nic Maddinson, who made a duck in the first innings on his return after a decade out of test cricket, played some expansive shots before Anrich Nortje clean bowled him for 48, and there were useful contributions from Beau Webster, 39 not out, and Cummins, who bludgeoned four sixes in his whirlwind 12-ball 32. Travis Head's 11 runs at the top of the Australia innings and 37 again from Marnus Labuschagne did not help their individual causes, although Labuschagne's 53-run partnership with Steve Smith (27) for the third wicket did accelerate the run rate and put Australia into an advantageous position. Smith was struck on the helmet by Nortje and is being assessed under concussion protocols. He batted on after the hit but did not join the rest of the Australian team on the field at the start of South Africa's chase and could be a doubt for the second test, which starts in Gqeberha on Sunday.

item.title: Papa León ingresará el martes al hospital para someterse a intervención quirúrgica: Vaticano
item.description: El Papa León ingresará en el hospital el martes para someterse a una intervención quirúrgica destinada a extirpar un pequeño nódulo detectado en un pulmón, informó el Vaticano, mientras el pontífice mantuvo una apretada agenda el lunes, celebrando por la mañana siete reuniones programadas con antelación.
item.dc:creator: Joshua McElwee
item.content:encoded: El Papa León ingresará en el hospital el martes para someterse a una intervención quirúrgica destinada a extirpar un pequeño nódulo detectado en un pulmón, informó el Vaticano, mientras el pontífice mantuvo una apretada agenda el lunes, celebrando por la mañana siete reuniones programadas con antelación. León, de 71 años, declaró el domingo que el nódulo se había detectado en un chequeo reciente, que estaba "bien delimitado" y que se había detectado a tiempo. El nódulo se detectó durante un chequeo médico rutinario, informó la oficina de prensa del Vaticano a primera hora del lunes, antes de confirmar que se espera que el Papa sea ingresado a última hora de la mañana del martes, antes de la intervención quirúrgica. No se especificó cuándo tendría lugar la operación propiamente dicha. El comunicado habitual sobre la agenda diaria del Papa, publicado el lunes al mediodía (1000 GMT), indicaba que se había reunido esa mañana con obispos visitantes de Argentina, Nicaragua y Estados Unidos, entre otros. En una reunión celebrada el lunes en el Vaticano con miembros de una organización benéfica con sede en Roma, el Papa habló con voz firme, agradeciéndoles su labor. León ha cancelado todos los actos públicos que tenía programados hasta el 20 de octubre, informó el Vaticano. León, elegido papa por los cardenales de todo el mundo en mayo de 2025, es relativamente joven para ser un líder de la Iglesia. Le gustan los deportes, incluido el tenis, y no se sabe que sea fumador ni que haya tenido problemas de salud anteriormente. El Vaticano ha indicado que se espera que la recuperación del Papa dure aproximadamente una semana. Un nódulo pulmonar es una pequeña lesión localizada que puede ser benigna. Según la Sociedad Torácica Americana, menos del 5% de los nódulos pulmonares resultan ser cancerosos, aunque el riesgo aumenta con la edad, el tamaño y otros factores como el tabaquismo. El doctor Federico Venuto, jefe de cirugía torácica del hospital Policlínico Umberto I de Roma, explicó que las intervenciones quirúrgicas para extirpar nódulos pulmonares suelen ser mínimamente invasivas y, en ocasiones, pueden implicar el uso de un tubo con cámara delgada denominado toracoscopio. "La tasa de complicaciones es extremadamente baja", declaró a Reuters. León, líder de una Iglesia que cuenta con 1.400 millones de fieles, tenía varias citas públicas en su agenda para esta semana, incluida una misa en la Plaza de San Pedro el miércoles por la mañana. El Vaticano no ha confirmado si la misa, que cierra una asamblea de obispos de una semana de duración, aún se celebrará. Aunque el Papa ingresará en el hospital el martes, la misa podría ser oficiada por un cardenal del Vaticano. León, de 71 años, dijo el domingo que el pequeño nódulo se había detectado en un chequeo reciente, que estaba "bien delimitado" y que se había encontrado a tiempo. El nódulo se detectó durante un chequeo médico rutinario, confirmó el lunes la oficina de prensa del Vaticano.

item.title: ノーベル経済学賞、米大教授2人に 経済安定化の研究
item.description: ［ストックホルム １２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ストックホルム　１２日　ロイター］ - スウェーデン王立科学アカデミーは１２日、２０２６年のノーベル経済学賞を米スタンフォード大学のロバート・ホール教授（８３）と米コロンビア大学のマイケル・ウッドフォード教授（７０）に授与すると発表した。授賞理由は「マクロ経済の安定化に関するミクロ経済学的基盤」。

両氏は、効果的な安定化政策を実行する能力を向上させる新たなボトムアップ型の経済モデルを開発した。これにより、経済に打撃を与える変動の激しさを緩和できる、適切なタイミングでの財政・金融政策の実施が可能となり、世界の中央銀行や財務省で活用されている。

経済学賞選考委員会のジョン・ハスラー委員長は声明で「両氏の功績は、現在世界中の各中央銀行や政府によって使われているモデルに安定した理論的基盤を提供した」と指摘。「両氏のモデルによって、エネルギー危機や家計消費の急変動など、経済へのショックにより適切に対処できるようになった」と述べた。

両氏の重要な洞察の一つは、経済の仕組みを上から捉えるトップダウン型の理論に頼るのではなく、家計や企業がミクロのレベルで下す無数の決定を考慮して初めて経済を安定させられるという点だ。

ウッドフォード氏は会見で「当局は、経済の安定化を、経済の中にいる人々がそれをどう理解しているかとは関係なく、誰かがレバーを引いて経済を操作するだけの作業と見なすべきではない」と語った。

ウッドフォード氏によると、中銀が高騰するインフレへの対応に苦しんだ１９７０年代の石油危機とは違い、２０００年代後半の世界金融危機では、新たな枠組みが伝統的な金融政策手段を補う上で役に立った。

「すぐに追加利下げできることだけに頼るのではなく、金利政策が今後どうなりそうかをより明確に表明することが、０９年以降の政策対応の重要な部分を占めた」と述べた。

両氏の研究は、金融政策の先行きを示す、いわゆる「フォワードガイダンス」のほかにも、需要が変化しても価格の変化が遅れる「粘着的な」インフレ、「需給ギャップ（アウトプットギャップ）」といった現在使われている概念を広めた。

item.title: Bardella antisemitism dispute tests French far right's decade-long makeover
item.description: Joseph Martin saw his hopes of becoming a far-right National Rally (RN) lawmaker derailed in 2024 after journalists unearthed a seemingly antisemitic post.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Pineau, Michel Rose
item.content:encoded: Joseph Martin saw his hopes of becoming a far-right National Rally (RN) lawmaker derailed in 2024 after journalists unearthed a seemingly antisemitic post. It was RN president Jordan Bardella who initially withdrew support for [USN:L1N3UP0GG TEXT:"Martin's candidacy"], seeking to show [USN:L8N3J31HH TEXT:"zero tolerance"] for antisemitism as [USN:L8N3IN1AQ TEXT:"the party tried"] to convince voters it had shed its toxic past and was ready for top office. So as the RN closes ranks around Bardella while he grapples with his own accusations of antisemitism – which he denies – Martin said the RN chief should be held to the same standard and step aside while the claims are investigated. "He judged me, condemned me and excluded me from the RN," said Martin, who was eventually cleared to run after the RN agreed his post was not antisemitic. However, he lost and saw his subsequent application to represent the party in future votes rejected, essentially ending his political career. The discrepancy between how the RN handled accusations against the two men - one the rising star of the party and the other a little-known regional candidate - raises questions about one of its most fundamental claims: that it has decisively broken with the [USN:L8N3CE2UV TEXT:"antisemitism"] that marked parts of its history. "There's been packaging, cosmetics and strategy, but the ideas persist," said Sciences-Po university political scientist Gilles Ivaldi. BARDELLA STANDS HIS GROUND Bardella has denied the allegations by investigative outlet Mediapart, which published purported antisemitic and conspiratorial comments he made in chats as a teenager, calling them "crude fakes" and saying he would file defamation lawsuits. Still, the scandal represents the gravest threat yet to the 31-year-old's rapid political ascent, while also posing a headache for RN presidential candidate Marine Le Pen as she seeks to win the presidency after three failed attempts. Le Pen, who leads polls ahead of next year's vote, has led a decade-long rebrand of the RN, while Bardella has visited Israel to show the party is free of the antisemitism for which its founder, Marine's father Jean-Marie Le Pen, was convicted. "This affair shines a harsh light on what the National Rally really is," said Socialist lawmaker Guillaume Garot. However, he also acknowledged the controversy was competing for attention with a long list of voter concerns, from high school protests and a weak economy to geopolitics. ALLEGATIONS MAY HURT LE PEN IN RUN-OFF VOTE The RN has rallied to Bardella's defence, while also playing down the scandal. "I think it has absolutely no impact on the ground whatsoever," Le Pen aide Renaud Labaye told Reuters. Some 74% of the French believe the messages are problematic if true, according to an IFOP poll for LCI TV, but only 21% say their opinion of Bardella has deteriorated. Bardella struck a defiant tone when challenged by a Mediapart journalist at a press conference last week. "Your little operation doesn't seem to be cutting through," he said. "You'd have loved to see me on my knees, but you clearly don't know me very well." Ivaldi said the RN's most loyal voters were unlikely to abandon the party as their priorities were purchasing power, energy prices, immigration and crime. But the scandal could hurt Le Pen in a run-off, when victory would depend on attracting conservative voters beyond the RN's traditional base. "If there is an impact, it is more likely to be among second-round voters, particularly those who pay closer attention to the RN's ideological profile," he said. INTERNAL TENSIONS The controversy comes at a delicate moment in the relationship between Le Pen and her protege Bardella, who had been the party's de facto presidential candidate until a Paris appeals court cleared her to run in a [USN:L6N4380IL TEXT:"shock July ruling"]. Bardella had increasingly asserted his independence in the run-up to that verdict, and party officials said frictions have since grown, including over the RN's rapprochement with Le Pen's niece, Marion Maréchal, an anti-abortion firebrand and potential Bardella rival. RN Senator Joshua Hochart played down the tensions but said Bardella was willing to make his disagreement known. "Bardella isn't just Marine Le Pen's protégé. His views count and he's right to say when something isn't working," he said. Although Le Pen has backed Bardella over the antisemitism claims, political rivals and analysts say he has been weakened. "The case complicates Marine Le Pen's campaign," Ivaldi said. "He is no longer the major asset he was for her." And in a party with a long history of sidelining ambitious politicians from outside the Le Pen clan, Bardella's future remains uncertain, Ivaldi said. Eric Zemmour, a former presidential candidate from the extreme-right Reconquest party, was blunt about Bardella's diminished status. "Jordan Bardella is in the process of being marginalized from the heart of the RN," he said on RTL radio on Monday, predicting he would now never become Le Pen's prime minister. "It's finished all that."

item.title: Most Americans oppose betting on elections, government events, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds
item.description: Most Americans oppose using prediction markets to bet on US elections and other government actions, according to a Reuters/Ipsos opinion poll that suggests the booming markets may lack broad public support as policymakers debate how to regulate them.
item.dc:creator: Chris Prentice, Jason Lange
item.content:encoded: Most Americans oppose using prediction markets to bet on US elections and other government actions, according to a Reuters/Ipsos opinion poll that suggests the booming markets may lack broad public support as policymakers debate how to regulate them. The [USN:L4N42Y0WQ TEXT:"rapidly growing prediction market industry"] led by Polymarket and Kalshi allows people to bet on a raft of events, including US elections, government policy moves and sports games, raising concerns among policymakers that the platforms are opening up new avenues for [USN:L6N44E0TQ TEXT:"insider trading"] and manipulation. The companies say they have [USN:L4N42H1L3 TEXT:"extensive controls"] to guard against misconduct, that their markets are often better at forecasting outcomes than traditional polls, and that they [USN:L6N44L0X4 TEXT:"offer unique ways to hedge"] a range of esoteric real-world risks. Yet a bipartisan majority of Americans is opposed to using prediction markets to bet on US elections , military actions and government policy announcements or decisions, according to the Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted September 30 through October 5. Some 69% of Democrats and 61% of Republicans said they opposed using prediction markets to bet on election results. Sixty-five percent of Americans opposed prediction market betting on US military actions and 63% opposed betting on government policy announcements or decisions, suggesting broad bipartisan discomfort with wagering on government affairs. Only 8% and 9%, respectively, supported such bets. The results shed more light on popular attitudes toward the nascent industry, which is marketing heavily on social media and TV even as it faces pushback from states and from Democratic lawmakers who argue the markets are unethical, socially corrosive and could undermine national security. "Everyone should make their own decisions about their lives," said Ronna Schmoker, 72, a Democrat from a Dallas suburb who participated in the poll. "But like anything, you have to have guardrails." A Polymarket spokesperson said Americans don't trust traditional information sources and that prediction markets help provide unbiased, accurate information. "It’s why more than 90% of visits to Polymarket are to view markets, not to trade," the spokesperson said. "Recognition of the public value of prediction markets is growing, but they’re still brand new to most, and it’s going to take some time for the public to learn more and see the real value." NATIONAL SECURITY AND ELECTION FEARS HAVE STOKED DEBATE Some policymakers worry that prediction markets, which offer thousands of ways to wager on the US midterms, [USN:L6N41V1AT TEXT:"could undermine faith in"] the integrity of US democracy and enable government insiders to broadcast confidential information via their trades. Reuters reported [USN:L6N44E0TQ TEXT:"in August"] that more than 150 accounts on Polymarket International, the company's overseas market which bars US users, may have traded on inside military information, while Kalshi [USN:L1N41514R TEXT:"has suspended candidates"] for betting on their own races. Kalshi banned former Republican congressman George Santos, who agreed to pay $35,000 [USN:L6N43X19K TEXT:"to resolve government allegations"] of manipulative trading after he bet via Kalshi on whether he would attend the State of the Union address. Santos did not admit to the allegations and said through his attorney that he never intended to deceive anyone. Ninety-three percent of Democrats and 89% of Republicans said it was inappropriate for members of Congress or their staff to bet on political events, while 6% and 8%, respectively, said it was appropriate. Polymarket and Kalshi say they work closely with the authorities and routinely refer suspicious accounts, and have introduced various restrictions to mitigate misconduct. Kalshi says it does not allow trading on military operations and bars political candidates from wagering on their own races. The Senate in April barred senators, staff and other officers from using prediction markets, and [USN:L4N4051K3 TEXT:"several Democratic lawmakers have introduced bills"] to restrict the industry. "We see prediction markets everywhere, but don't mistake seeing millions of dollars in advertisements as a sign of growing support," said Democratic Senator Jeff Merkley of Oregon. "Folks are rightfully concerned." The Reuters/Ipsos poll suggests many Americans are generally uneasy about increasingly commoditizing real-world events. Even betting on professional sports, a far more established activity, was opposed by 43% of respondents, while 29% supported it. "I just don't think it's good for a society to bet on whether things will turn out a certain way," said Michael Clark, a 48-year-old conservative who lives outside Dallas and participated in the poll. TRUMP ADMINISTRATION HAS SUPPORTED INDUSTRY GROWTH The administration of President Donald Trump, whose son Donald Trump Jr. has business ties to Kalshi and Polymarket, is pursuing federal regulations for the industry, a move states are fighting. Legal experts expect that dispute to reach the Supreme Court. At issue is whether prediction markets facilitate trading in financial instruments or gambling, which is regulated by the states. State regulators say they are facilitating gambling and should be subject to more stringent state laws, while Trump's Commodity Futures Trading Commission has asserted jurisdiction, arguing the contracts are a type of financial product it regulates. "By that rationale, MGM (Resorts) owns dozens of financial markets," said Glenn Rishton, a 76-year-old Republican poll respondent in Gulfport, Mississippi, referring to the casino company. "It's effectively gambling." Three-quarters of Americans agreed, with only 8% saying using prediction markets to wager on the outcome of real-world events is not a form of gambling. The Reuters/Ipsos poll, which was conducted online and nationwide, surveyed 4,506 US adults and had a margin of error of about two percentage points. "Prediction markets should have the same level of regulations as gambling," said Janessa Manning, 48, a Democrat in Detroit. "Even though they pretend they aren’t gambling, they are."

item.title: Kyiv says Russia hits energy targets despite Trump ceasefire announcement
item.description: Russia hit at least six energy targets during a night and morning of deadly airstrikes across Ukraine, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday, adding this showed Moscow had no interest in an energy ceasefire announced by Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Flynn, Pavel Polityuk
item.content:encoded: Russia hit at least six energy targets during a night and morning of deadly airstrikes across Ukraine, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday, adding this showed Moscow had no interest in an energy ceasefire announced by Donald Trump. Under pressure over high energy prices ahead of US midterm elections next month, US President Trump blindsided Kyiv and its European allies over the weekend by declaring that Ukraine and Russia had agreed not to hit each other's energy systems. "It is increasingly evident that Russia is unwilling to accept an energy ceasefire proposed by the United States and intends to continue its terrorist air attacks against our people and communities," Zelenskiy said on X. "This is what happens when Russia sees the prospect of higher revenues for its war machine." In earlier comments by video link to a conference in Poland, Zelenskiy identified two of the targets as a gas facility and a petrol station, both hit by Russian drones. Trump announced the purported energy ceasefire days after unveiling a [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"deal to buy diesel from Russia"], which Zelenskiy has criticised as a reversal of years of Western policy aimed at isolating Russia's economy. Trump, for his part, has called on Ukrainians to unseat Zelenskiy in an election, an unusually severe exchange in a relationship between the two leaders that has been strained since Trump returned to power in 2025. Trump's announcement was the second time within a few weeks that Trump has declared an energy ceasefire without confirmation from the two warring sides. Ukraine's European allies on Monday voiced scepticism of any such agreement, spoke strongly in support of Kyiv and [USN:L8N45T1J0 TEXT:"approved the largest set of EU sanctions"] since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. 'WE DO NOT WANT A CEASEFIRE,' KREMLIN SAYS Kyiv has increasingly targeted Russian oil refineries and logistics with long-range strikes in recent months, its answer to more than four-and-a-half years of relentless Russian attacks on its cities, including persistent campaigns to knock out Ukraine's power and heat in successive winters. Zelenskiy said Ukraine had carried out no attacks on Russian refineries overnight and was willing to agree an energy ceasefire, but only if Russia abided by it. He also said elections, suspended during wartime, could be held in Ukraine if Moscow agreed to a full ceasefire for 60 days. Russia, for its part, said talks were ongoing about a possible energy ceasefire, and Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said further information would be revealed in due course. But he rejected Zelenskiy's proposal for a full 60-day truce. "In the Kremlin, both President (Vladimir) Putin and officials at other levels have repeatedly stated that we do not want a ceasefire," said Peskov. "We want long-term peace and are prepared to do everything possible to achieve it." BODY AMONG WRECKAGE In Kharkiv, Ukraine's second biggest city, rescue workers picked through wreckage of shattered buildings. The body of a dead civilian in jeans and white sneakers lay beneath debris, lit up by floodlights in the nighttime dark. Nataliia Minka said she had just made it to a shelter when a missile struck nearby. She and her child had seen what they believed to be a missile hitting a nearby power station. “Ten minutes had passed since they promised they wouldn’t target energy facilities," she said. “It’s so hard to describe how a child was lying there, already covered up, and the father was running around her, crying and screaming," she added. "It’s so terrifying -- it’s impossible to get through something like this.” After nighttime attacks killed at least three people in Kharkiv, further strikes took place in the morning, hitting residential buildings and wounding at least 22 more people, municipal officials said. At least three other people were reported killed on Sunday in the western city of Ivano-Frankivsk. Russia began its latest strike campaign on Ukraine's grid two weeks ago, already causing daily, hours-long power cuts in Kyiv, affecting the capital's water and sewage systems and twice bringing its underground trains to an abrupt halt. To maintain pressure on Moscow, European Union foreign ministers on Monday added 1,569 new names to their sanctions list of banned individuals and businesses, billed as the largest single package to date. Germany's Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Moscow "will only negotiate seriously under pressure, which is why we are sticking to our sanctions against Russia. "Following Moscow's ruthless attacks on Ukraine's civilian energy infrastructure, we must actually tighten them further." Trump has increasingly blamed Kyiv's attacks on Russian refineries for surging global costs for fuel, especially diesel, which has hit record prices in the United States since he launched his military campaign against Iran. On Saturday he said Zelenskiy had [USN:L6N45W06G TEXT:""better damn well stop""] attacking Russian refineries. A person familiar with the situation said the US had threatened to cut off intelligence sharing with Ukraine and supplies of weapons, which Washington no longer provides to Kyiv but allows European countries to buy on its behalf.

item.title: Pope Leo to be hospitalised on Tuesday ahead of lung surgery
item.description: Pope Leo will go into hospital on Tuesday for surgery to remove a small growth found on one of his lungs, the Vatican said, as the pontiff kept up a busy schedule on Monday, holding seven previously planned meetings in the morning.
item.dc:creator: Joshua McElwee
item.content:encoded: Pope Leo will go into hospital on Tuesday for surgery to remove a small growth found on one of his lungs, the Vatican said, as the pontiff kept up a busy schedule on Monday, holding seven previously planned meetings in the morning. Leo, 71, said [USN:L1N45X029 TEXT:"on Sunday"] that the growth, a small nodule, had been found on a recent check-up, was "well-contained" and had been spotted early. Ahead of his hospitalisation, the pope cancelled all his public events from Tuesday until October 20. The nodule was found during a routine health check, the Vatican press office told journalists earlier on Monday, before confirming that the pope is expected to be hospitalised late on Tuesday morning, ahead of his surgery. It did not say when the actual operation would take place. A regular advisory on the pope's daily schedule, issued at noon (1000 GMT) on Monday, said he met that morning with visiting bishops from Argentina, Nicaragua and the United States, among others. In a meeting at the Vatican with members of a Rome-based charity group on Monday, the pope spoke in a strong, clear voice, thanking them for their work. COMPLICATION RATE FOR NODULE REMOVAL LOW Leo, elected pope by the world's cardinals in May 2025, is relatively young for a Church leader. He enjoys sports, including tennis, and is not known to be a smoker or to have had health issues previously. The Vatican has said the pope's recovery is expected to take about a week. A nodule on the lung is a small, localised lesion that can be benign. The American Thoracic Society says fewer than 5% of lung nodules overall prove cancerous, although risk rises with age, size, and other factors such as smoking. Dr. Federico Venuto, chief of thoracic surgery at Rome's Policlinico Umberto I hospital, said surgeries to remove lung nodules are usually minimally invasive, and can sometimes involve use of a thin camera tube called a thoracoscope. "The complication rate is extremely low," he told Reuters. POPE'S TRANSPARENCY ABOUT HEALTH UNUSUAL Leo's decision to discuss his upcoming surgery publicly on Sunday marked a contrast with his predecessor, the late Pope Francis, who died in April 2025 at age 88. Francis was hospitalised several times as he grew frail in his later years and did not usually announce his hospital visits in advance, sometimes sparking a media frenzy over his health. Canadian Cardinal Gérald Lacroix said on Monday that he was grateful for Leo's transparency. "I really appreciated yesterday ... (that) he himself said, 'This is what's going on,' very transparent, and asked for prayers," said Lacroix. "I like that." Leo, the leader of the 1.4-billion-member Church, had several public appointments on his calendar for this week, including a Mass in St. Peter's Square on Wednesday morning. The Vatican said the Mass would now be led by Filipino Cardinal Luis Tagle, a Vatican official whom Leo [USN:L8N45V0O6 TEXT:"last week"] approved as the dean of the Church's College of Cardinals, in the first selection of an Asian cleric to the elite role. In the event of a papal death or resignation, the dean of the cardinals is responsible for organizing the secret conclave to elect his successor. The pope is the final earthly authority for the world's Catholics and does not have a deputy who steps in when he is sick. When a pope is incapacitated, the business of the Vatican's vast bureaucracy carries on as usual, holding off on any decisions that require papal approval.

item.title: パキスタン、カーン元首相派の州首相ら拘束 非常事態宣言
item.description:
Asif Shahzad
［イスラマバード １２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Asif Shahzad

［イスラマバード　１２日　ロイター］ - パキスタン連邦政府は１２日、北西部カイバル・パクトゥンクワ州のアフリディ州首相らを拘束したと明らかにした。アフリディ氏は収監中のカーン元首相の政党「パキスタン正義運動（ＰＴＩ）」に所属する。ザルダリ大統領は１１日、同州政府がイスラム過激派対策を怠っているとして非常事態を宣言し、州政府の権限を停止した。

チョードリー内務担当国務相はロイターに対し、「州首相と一部の州閣僚が予防拘禁されたことを確認できる」と述べた。拘束は１１日、同州北西部の都市ペシャワルにある州首相公邸で行われたという。訴追すべき案件がある者は起訴して裁判にかけ、それ以外の者は釈放すると述べた。

州首相公邸と周辺の重要施設には多数の警察官と準軍事組織の部隊が配置され、輸送用コンテナで封鎖されている。

同州では１週間前、ＰＴＩ支持者による集会が数日にわたって開かれ、支持者らは、カーン氏の釈放と治療を求めてイスラマバードへ行進する予定だった。

政府とＰＴＩは、９月にデモ行進が呼びかけられて以降、数回にわたって協議を重ねてきた。

チョードリー氏は、政府はデモ行進の容認を含め、ＰＴＩの要求を全て受け入れる用意があったと説明し、「われわれが求めたのはただ一つ、党が武装勢力を公に非難し、武装勢力との戦いでわれわれと手を携えることだった」と述べた。ＰＴＩは同意せず、協議は決裂したという。

item.title: UK proposes rewards for whistleblowers who report economic crimes
item.description: Britain's Serious Fraud Office is developing plans to reward whistleblowers who report economic crimes such as fraud and bribery, the government said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Phoebe Seers
item.content:encoded: Britain's Serious Fraud Office is developing plans to reward whistleblowers who report economic crimes such as fraud and bribery, the government said on Monday. The move would bring Britain closer to the US model, where financial incentives have been used to encourage people to come forward with evidence of wrongdoing for more than a decade. Britain has for years debated whether to pay whistleblowers for information. Last year, the tax authority HM Revenue & Customs [USN:L1N3X20S3 TEXT:"introduced the country's first US-style reward scheme"], offering informants up to 30% of tax recovered in major tax cases. The shift has been driven by the success of overseas programmes, particularly the US Securities and Exchange Commission's whistleblower regime, for which UK nationals are the second-largest overseas user group, the government said. "We welcome this consultation, having long called for the introduction of a scheme to incentivise whistleblowers. We encourage all those with a view to contribute to the consultation and we look forward to working with our government partners on next steps," a spokesperson for the SFO said. The change was recommended in a July 2026 review of fraud prosecutions led by lawyer Jonathan Fisher, who said Britain was losing valuable intelligence as whistleblowers chose to report wrongdoing to US authorities that offer financial rewards. Former SFO Director Nick Ephgrave said in 2024 that paying corporate insiders to provide "smoking gun evidence" could[USN:L5N3EY6O3 TEXT:" significantly increase the speed"] of investigations. Under proposals set out for public consultation, whistleblowers would be eligible for a reward only if they provide significant, original information that leads to a conviction or enforcement action. Mirroring the US approach, the government has proposed that rewards be funded from penalties imposed on companies and calculated as a percentage of the amount recovered. Eliza Lockhart, a senior research fellow at RUSI's Centre for Finance and Security, said rewards recognise whistleblowing as "the provision of an intelligence service" rather than simply an altruistic act. "If policymakers are serious about tackling economic crime, adopting an intelligence-led approach is crucial," Lockhart said. Eoin O'Shea, a partner at law firm CMS, said a reward-based system "seems reasonable in principle" given the risks whistleblowers can face, including dismissal or workplace discrimination. However, critics argue that offering financial rewards could encourage reports motivated by personal gain rather than the public interest. Jo Mackie, an employment partner at law firm Michelmores, said such incentives created a "moral hazard" and risked undermining internal corporate governance, adding that paying whistleblowers was "fundamentally flawed".

FAST

LONDON, Oct 12 : Artificial Intelligence needs urgent global regulation with independent evaluators able to vet new developments, the president of Microsoft said, warning that AI currently faces fewer safety requirements than milk.   In an interview with the BBC published on Monday, Brad Smith said a set of global safety rules needed to be in place, requiring a "victim" to be informed if their system is breached by a rogue AI agent and an "emergency brake" available. He said there should also be a legal requirement for companies to write "incident reports".  "We know how to do this for other products," Smith said. "We should build on that knowledge and think about how to apply it to AI."

"Right now, your washing machine is subject to more safety rules than AI. Every carton of milk that you see in the grocery store is subject to safety rules and inspection." Tech companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI have started disclosing rogue or undesired behaviour by AI agents as part of a global debate about the fast-advancing technology that has included researchers' warnings of an eventual existential threat to humanity. Some companies have called for AI development to slow down, but that has sparked a debate as to whether executives have ulterior motives such as setting rules that preserve the lead of their firms, pre-empting a broader government backlash, or simply slowing breakneck spending. Microsoft's Smith said the one country that was well-placed to lead the way on regulation of AI was Britain, due to the AI Security Institute which was launched under former prime minister, Rishi Sunak.  Smith said officials in Washington viewed London very differently to how they viewed Brussels, which regulates AI based on the level of risk via its AI Act. Britain's institute receives pre-deployment access under voluntary agreements with the major AI models, allowing it to assess their capabilities and risks.  AI Minister Kanishka Narayan has told Reuters that Britain would consider regulating advanced models if the current system proved insufficient.

FAST

NEW YORK/LONDON, Oct 12 : The dollar held near an 18-month high on Monday, supported by safe-haven demand as an escalating Middle East conflict kept investors cautious ahead of key US inflation data later this week. Oil prices were volatile after Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis stepped up strikes on Saudi Arabia, and two tankers were attacked over the weekend.  Brent crude futures rose 2.09 per cent to $106.80 a barrel, nearing a two-week high, as the attacks overshadowed Sunday's announcement from US President Donald Trump about an energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia. The futures price is still nearly 45 per cent above where it was before the US-Israeli war with Iran started. The dollar index, which tracks the US currency against six others, was up 0.16 per cent at 102.39, just below last week's 18-month high.

Weekly data from the US markets regulator shows investors have been adding to their bullish positions on the dollar, which rose to around $36 billion in the week to October 7 from $8.4 billion three weeks ago, largely at the expense of the euro. "Markets got off to a relatively encouraging start to the week, but sentiment has since deteriorated as renewed geopolitical uncertainty and rising oil prices weigh on risk appetite, prompting a fresh round of US dollar demand," said Joel Kruger, a market strategist at LMAX Group in London. SPOTLIGHT MOVES TO US INFLATION DATA  Wednesday's US consumer inflation report, one of the last major economic releases before the Federal Reserve's policy meeting this month, could be critical in determining the near-term direction of the dollar.  Data last week showed US consumer sentiment deteriorated further in early October, as the rising cost of living because of the Middle East conflict soured households' views of the economy. The Fed raised rates last month for the first time since 2023 to rein in inflation, with markets keeping a close watch on economic data to gauge whether policymakers may move again. Traders are pricing in an 81 per cent chance of the Fed standing pat this month, up from 51 per cent a month earlier, the CME FedWatch tool showed. "The real focus is on the CPI number this week, it is likely to be running hot," said Marc Chandler, chief market strategist at Bannockburn Global Forex in New York. He added that a rate hike before an election is so uncommon that "the bar is kind of high" for the Fed to act. Sharp selloffs in bond markets in the past few weeks worried investors as borrowing costs across the globe rose to multi-decade highs on concern over inflation, energy prices and ballooning government debt.  The euro fell 0.19 per cent to $1.1180, after clocking a fifth straight week of losses last week, driven by investor angst around France's fiscal health before the 2027 presidential election. The spread between French 10-year yields and safer German yields traded at 140 basis points. Last week it neared 160 bps, the most since 2012. "It is still too early to tell whether higher borrowing costs will be sufficient to impose greater fiscal discipline on the French government," said OCBC FX strategists.  Against the yen, the US dollar was a touch higher on the day at 158.57 yen in holiday-thinned trading in Japan, while the pound held steady at $1.323.

Source: Reuters
